title: Experiment disposition rollup
description: Summarize every A-W C0-C10 and added X-Y experiment as promoted rejected or inconclusive, with hypothesis, oracle, cells, threshold, kill criterion, and retained artifact references.
acceptance_criteria: No speculative bead lacks an evidence-backed disposition; promoted code has dispatch and regression gates; losers leave concise reports rather than default dead code.

title: Final mission evidence report and source appendix
description: Produce the plan.md section 22 final report with branch commits Beads API profiles compatibility tests sanitizers fuzz benchmarks scaling memory experiments limitations repro commands and exact source URLs.
acceptance_criteria: All fourteen required report sections are evidence-backed; plan and Beads graph reconcile; repository and issue graph are clean.

title: Final 1-to-128 scaling and NUMA campaign
description: Run isolated 1 2 4 8 16 32 64 128 thread scaling, affinity, bandwidth saturation, and NUMA experiments using completed scheduler and benchmark infrastructure. Split local 32-CPU evidence from external 128-CPU validation.
acceptance_criteria: Machine-readable results report aggregate input and output throughput, setup, confidence, topology, affinity, memory bandwidth saturation, and reasons for unavailable cells.

title: Continuous correctness and differential infrastructure
description: Maintain fast independent-oracle, randomized, exhaustive-small, guard, compatibility, and backend-differential tests usable throughout production and experiments. Final campaign disposition remains in leopard-79h.15.
acceptance_criteria: Deterministic sharded tests run locally and through the lab runner, log seeds and counts, and can gate experimental tasks before the final campaign.
notes: Evidence commits 35dc1df and 5e4b982 provide deterministic public-API fuzz smoke, opt-in upstream-Clang libFuzzer, seed/case/thread sharding, backend matrix, and a permanent boundary differential. Current combined gates: Release 11/11, ASan+UBSan 11/11, random seed 903176249 with 2,048 patterns/4,096 repeats/24,962 recovered/4,452 generic comparisons, boundary 108 cases/432 executions/1,572 recovered, and auto/scalar/SSSE3/AVX2 golden+API+64-case random with matching output hashes and runtime backend assertions. Prior 128 independent release seeds x2,048 (262,144) passed. Actual coverage-guided fuzzing remains blocked by absent upstream clang; GCC rejects the option clearly.

title: GF16 arbitrary positive byte tails
description: Remove the current GF16 multiple-of-64 limitation without truncating ALTMAP high halves. Define safe tail staging for encode and decode in the new API while preserving the old API contract.
acceptance_criteria: Required boundary byte sizes including 1 through 65 and 1023 through 1025 pass GF16 direct differential, guards, ASan and UBSan; no wire change.
notes:
Parallel wave: establish information-theoretic and representation constraints for arbitrary GF16 byte tails, then implement every safe in-profile case or document required API/profile change.
Evidence commit d748620: production compact GF16 tail scatter/gather accepts every positive even length while preserving complete 64-byte ALTMAP tiles and zero-copy multiples. High parity matches packed legacy; low parity matches independent generator; high/low specialized/generic decode, R=1/K=1, strict, 8/8 Release, 8/8 ASan+UBSan, and 32x512 differentials pass. Independent oracle checked 360,192 recovered symbols. Odd lengths remain LEO2_UNSUPPORTED: docs/leopard2_gf16_tails.md proves a fixed-B-byte universal contract impossible via the q-1 MOLS bound for K=2,R=256,B=1 and gives executable rank-14 rows 0,256 collision. Full arbitrary-positive semantics require a separately versioned padded/hybrid/paired profile, so this bead remains open rather than falsely meeting its original acceptance.

title: Baseline compatibility and instrumentation completion
description: Complete Milestone 0 gaps after the initial baseline: raw recoverable golden parity and outputs, scalar SSSE3 AVX2 and testable NEON determinism, all host-supported builds, and field-add multiply memory-pass and butterfly instrumentation.
acceptance_criteria: Artifacts and commands cover each supported backend and field; compact raw vectors are committed; instrumentation separates algorithmic from ISA changes.
notes:
Evidence 0bd6892 freezes 960 raw legacy parity bytes for 5 GF8/GF16 vectors, independently regenerated at baseline SHA 3492b974 and current sources; aggregate SHA256 6973b1ec2b02ab7d171b8c7ed3a8281ea744896ca66805c2544aef4884bebafe, with 1,920 recovered bytes. Evidence 5e4b982 adds forced scalar/SSSE3/AVX2 builds: all three plus auto passed the frozen vectors, public API and random suite with identical stdout/stderr hashes, and forced runs asserted runtime backend identity. Boundary differential passed 108 profile/byte cases, 432 specialized/generic executions, 1,572 recovered shards, and field-inflation rejection. Native NEON evidence and full operation instrumentation remain.
Checkpoint evidence f742538 adds deterministic ISA-independent operation instrumentation for high/low encode, specialized/generic decode, generic transform, and bounded direct repair. Self-test passed 327 invariants and the independent suite passed 8/8. Metrics distinguish exact schedules and scratch from bounded skew/direct arithmetic and estimated logical traffic. Native NEON and hardware-counter evidence remain.

title: Documentation and release readiness
description: Document API, wire profiles, migration, limitations, sources, results, reproducer commands, promoted/rejected experiments, and ensure clean reviewable local commits.

title: Correctness, sanitizers, fuzzing, and compatibility
description: Run exhaustive MDS, GF8/GF16 differential, legacy golden, buffer/alias/guard, ASan/UBSan/TSan/MSan where supported, 128-seed fuzz, and deterministic stress campaigns.
notes: TSan build completed but every executable aborts before user code with FATAL: ThreadSanitizer: unexpected memory mapping on this host; recorded as a GCC TSan runtime/environment blocker, not a clean concurrency result. Release and ASan+UBSan randomized evidence continues independently. XDRS differential commit ce1cc84 explicitly invoked low Algorithm 2 and high Algorithm 3 at upstream SHA ae05a779e7f44be13c3d34e14d15b08b4bc02404: all 9 cases recovered 4 originals in both XDRS and Leopard2. Every parity row differed after symbol-basis conversion because upstream active coordinate order is polynomial-prefix while Leopard is Cantor-prefix; docs/leopard2_xdrs_differential.md records this expected code-definition difference and reproduction.

title: Benchmark and experiment harness
description: Build resumable affinity-aware deterministic JSON job runner and fair old/new/direct/high/low setup/execution benchmarks with counters and confidence statistics.
notes: Partial evidence: commit ea295f1 adds deterministic affinity/topology-aware resumable lab runner. Current work adds benchmark JSON with setup/execution/reuse, throughput, scratch, legacy comparison, and cost-model C0 integration. Full benchmark matrix remains.

title: SIMD and runtime backend refactor
description: Refactor scalar/SSSE3/AVX2/native-NEON primitives behind safe runtime dispatch; add self-tests, arbitrary tails, and isolated optional ISA experiments.
notes: Evidence commit 5e4b982 adds diagnostic target-local LEO2_BACKEND_VARIANT=auto|scalar|ssse3|avx2 without changing default auto. Four isolated Release builds passed frozen golden, API, and fixed-seed random tests with identical stdout/stderr hashes; each forced API run additionally asserted runtime backend introspection equals the requested scalar/SSSE3/AVX2 value. Combined direct-repair tree passed 11/11 Release and ASan+UBSan. Invalid values fail configuration. Matrix is affinity-aware/resumable and records deterministic JSON under ignored results/leopard2/backend-matrix. Production native NEON and broader backend refactor remain.

title: 128-core batch, scheduler, and NUMA work
description: Add batch APIs, persistent/caller executor model, per-worker scratch, affinity-aware scheduling, NUMA partition experiments, and 1..128 scaling where hardware permits.
notes: Current implementation adds a persistent context-owned batch pool with deterministic error selection and no per-call thread creation. Local 1..32 measurements show memory saturation; affinity/NUMA and external 128-CPU work remain.

title: Reusable erasure-plan API and locator strategies
description: Implement immutable reusable decode-plan semantics, deterministic survivor selection, locator setup strategies, permanent puncture contributions, pruned schedules, fixed factors, output scatter, and concurrency safety on top of the core API.
notes:
Partial evidence: commit 5cf1680 adds immutable locator plans and prepared generic execution; current work adds virtual survivor selection, fixed specialized factors, and reused batch execution. Locator strategy/pruning breadth remains.
Parallel wave: audit and improve parent-size locator/fixed-factor setup and reusable-plan memory/cost without changing erasure semantics.
Evidence commit 785c686: immutable codecs now own permanent erasure masks and specialized fixed factors; adaptive sparse direct XOR-index locator setup retains the FWHT reference and reuses permanent locator contributions only in the measured direct region. Test compares 327,108 locator entries and 256 concurrent preparations. Release/strict/ASan+UBSan/random gates passed. GF16 N=2048 sparse plan setup measured about 4.2us; dense Walsh remains about 150us by design.

title: Direct small-loss recovery
description: Implement no-loss no-op, R=1 XOR, tiny direct matrix paths, and LxL small-loss solver with deterministic dispatcher thresholds.
notes: Evidence commits 5cf1680 and ec1d57a complete the production scope: true no-loss no-op, R=1 XOR, K=1 direct copy, and bounded general LxL repair for 2<=K<=16, L<=4, parent dimension<=256. Codec-time legacy-Cantor barycentric weights include shortened systematic coordinates; immutable plans select lowest available parity rows, invert LxL, prune zero coefficients, and execute allocation-free with SIMD full tiles plus GF8 arbitrary/GF16 compact-even tails. Independent direct oracle evidence in 0bd6892 covered 50 GF4 profiles, 2,120 plans, 1,113,915 executions and 1,989,902 recovered symbols. Combined Release and ASan+UBSan 11/11, 2,048 random patterns/24,962 recovered, boundary 108 cases, and scalar/SSSE3/AVX2 determinism passed. Independent pinned review: high GF8 K16/R8/L1 1.094us direct vs 11.527us generic, 640 vs 230,528 scratch; low GF16 K16/R240/L4 79.118us vs 1305.691us, 4,352 vs 33,562,880 scratch. docs/leopard2_direct_repair.md. Bead remains in progress only because blocking plan task leopard-79h.11 is open.

title: Leopard2 public API and wire identity
description: Own the Leopard2 context, codec, core C ABI, profile and field identity, scratch and alias contracts, batch surface, serialized-code identity boundary, and API-completion gate. Decode-plan locator implementation is owned by leopard-79h.11.
notes: Partial evidence: commit 5cf1680 adds leopard2.h context, codec, scratch, encode, decode, batch, profile/field introspection, aliases, tails, and errors. GF16 arbitrary tails and serialized identity remain.

title: Arbitrary counts via shortening and puncturing
description: Support all legal positive K,R through declared high/low parent constructions, including R>K and safe GF8/GF16 boundary selection.
notes:
Partial evidence: commit 5cf1680 implements arbitrary public counts using the documented high and low shortening/puncturing maps; wider boundary and exact-field-rescue gates remain.
Checkpoint evidence 5e4b982 and 09d25e1: permanent boundary differential covers 108 high/low cases and 432 specialized/generic executions across GF8/GF16, including R>K and field-inflation rejection; active-transform differential adds 44 profiles and 32,094 byte comparisons. Exact GF8 field-boundary rescue remains experimental.

title: Low-rate encoder and profile
description: Implement versioned low profile using P=ceil_pow2(K), shifted P-point evaluation, shortening/puncturing, R>K, requested parity subsets, and systematic/MDS tests.
notes:
Partial evidence: commit 5cf1680 implements the versioned low profile, shifted P-point encode, R greater than K, subsets, and direct-oracle tests; maximum-count/performance/streaming gates remain.
Coordinator wave: reduce low-profile aligned-input/output copies and scratch footprint, add tiny direct thresholds only with direct-oracle and pinned whole-codec evidence.
Evidence commit 785c686: aligned low encode reads/writes caller buffers directly and stages only GF8 partial tiles. Release/strict/ASan+UBSan and random gates passed. Pinned K=32,R=224,64KiB improved 1474us to 975-1008us; scratch fell from about 21MB to 4,200,960 bytes. GF16 compact tails, maximum-count, tiny direct and streaming gates remain.

title: Low-rate decoder
description: Implement and validate IT2026 Algorithm 4 for the active low-profile parent, separating pattern setup from byte execution.
notes: Current implementation in a274d61 adds active-parent IT2026 Algorithm 4 original-only recovery with cached block factors and generic fallback. Exhaustive small high/low subsets and broad GF8/GF16 default-vs-generic differentials pass. Performance commit 7b71817 pinned CPU0, 64 KiB, batch1: low K16 R240 loss8 specialized 27.03 offered GB/s versus generic 12.83 (110.6% faster); plan setup medians 1.17 and 1.15 us. XDRS upstream low Algorithm2 at SHA ae05a77 independently recovered four originals for K=8,16,32,64,128; its polynomial-prefix coordinate profile is intentionally not parity-compatible with Leopard's Cantor-prefix profile (ce1cc84).

title: Legacy high-rate encoder
description: Add planned legacy-compatible high-rate encode with arbitrary tails, requested parity subsets, zero/puncture pruning, scratch queries, and bit-identical parity gates.
notes:
Partial evidence: commit 5cf1680 implements legacy-compatible high encode, arbitrary GF8 tails, parity subsets, scratch and alias contracts; broad compatibility/performance/direct-path gates remain.
Parallel wave: eliminate avoidable aligned-input copies and close high-encoder regression while retaining tails, subsets, bit identity and no hot allocation.
Evidence commit 785c686: zero-copy aligned high encode, direct requested parity outputs, requested-suffix pruning, all-null parity no-op, and XORSummer R=1 path. Release/strict/ASan+UBSan and deterministic random gates passed. Pinned K=240,R=16,64KiB encode 927us to 676-696us with scratch reduced to 2,103,424 bytes; new 22.58 GB/s vs legacy 22.84 GB/s on CPU0. GF16 compact tails and streaming/direct-tiny work remain.

title: Legacy-compatible high-rate decoder
description: Implement and validate IT2026 Algorithm 5 active-parent message-only recovery with reusable setup and generic fallback.
notes: Current implementation in a274d61 adds active-parent IT2026 Algorithm 5 message-only recovery with cached c_n normalization and generic fallback. Gates passed 6,620 default-vs-generic patterns, exhaustive small subsets, active GF16 N through 4096, and native AVX2 ASan+UBSan. Performance commit 7b71817 pinned CPU0, 64 KiB, batch1: high K240 R16 loss2 specialized 15.34 offered GB/s versus generic 7.69 (99.6% faster); balanced K128 R128 loss8 specialized 8.06 versus generic 7.78 (3.5% faster), with no neighboring regression. XDRS upstream high Algorithm3 at SHA ae05a77 independently recovered four originals for K=192,224,240,248; its polynomial-prefix coordinate profile is intentionally not parity-compatible with Leopard's Cantor-prefix profile (ce1cc84).

It passes strict-warning Release, ASan+UBSan, and forced auto/scalar/SSSE3/AVX2 backend variants. Broader production pruned-schedule work remains.

acceptance_criteria: Default configure does not probe CUDA; opt-in syntax and limitations are documented; enabled-without-toolkit failure is actionable.
notes: Initial uncommitted evidence: README_CUDA.md and LEO2_ENABLE_CUDA=OFF gate; default configuration never calls enable_language(CUDA). Canonical project option is -DLEO2_ENABLE_CUDA=ON because literal cmake --enable-cuda is not valid CMake syntax.

acceptance_criteria: All child tasks have correctness or documented negative-result evidence; default CPU configure/build/install has no CUDA dependency; final promotion decision is evidence-based.

title: Experiment C0: symbolic cost and dependency simulator
description:
Hypothesis: The symbolic cost and dependency simulator stage can reduce padded computation or define a useful separately versioned exact profile.
Implementation plan: Implement the specified staged scalar model/candidate before optimized kernels; preserve distinction between wire-compatible computation and new code identities.
Correctness oracle: Full padded transform for compatible work; independent direct algebra and exhaustive small-field MDS for exact profiles.
Benchmark cells: All GF8 K,R<=256 plus representative GF16, power boundaries, bytes, batch, and reuse.
Promotion threshold: >=10% meaningful-region measured gain, required identity/MDS gates, deterministic dispatcher.
Kill criterion: Dense joins, setup, memory traffic, complexity, or wire mismatch erase the benefit.
Final result: pending.
notes:
Current cost_model.py implements nine candidate models and deterministic CSV/JSONL schema. Full 1..256 sweep produced 1,179,648 rows with SHA-256 323324abf66a805d33634b62838b0d47885f6766af3c3a156699c80e0142fae6; awaiting commit.
Evidence commit 18227fc: deterministic symbolic simulator with nine methods, correctness classes, memory and arithmetic metrics, stable CSV/JSONL, stale-output cleanup, and self-test registered in CTest.
Checkpoint evidence 92faec9: C0 v2 independently models 65,536 public (K,R) pairs, 131,072 profile cells, and 1,048,576 method rows. Self-test passed 1,440 dependency networks and 4,896 cost-row invariants. Full 32-worker and independent 7-worker runs reproduced all retained artifacts, 16 heat maps, and the 24,312,909-byte full matrix byte-for-byte (SHA-256 938d12d58a563c2a3843da54c384b269dd679881f188469099bdecf362a73e39). Parent-preserving C1 pruning and C6/D GF8 boundary rescue are the top follow-ups.

Benchmark cells: Cache-hot/cold, consumer timing, large shards.
Promotion threshold: >=5% end-to-end without consumer regressions.

title: Experiment P: incremental parity updates
description:
Hypothesis: Delta updates beat full encode for few changed sources/ranges.

Benchmark cells: Tiny shards, latency, batch threshold, ISAs.

description:

Benchmark cells: RS(255,223), error counts, setup/execution.

description:

title: Experiment L: offline autotuning
description:
Hypothesis: Deterministic offline tables improve dispatch across regions.

Promotion threshold: Avoid >=5% losses and no >2% unexplained neighbors.

title: Experiment M: checksum-assisted corruption-to-erasure
description:
Hypothesis: External validation can convert known corruptions into fast erasures.

Benchmark cells: Validation cost, batch sizes, corruption rates.

title: Experiment J: plan cache and fixed-pattern batching
description:

title: Experiment K: NUMA task graph
description:
Hypothesis: Per-node pools and first touch reduce cross-node traffic.

Promotion threshold: >=10% aggregate gain on multi-node host.

description:

Benchmark cells: Counts 257..4096, shard and batch sweep.

Kill criterion: No clear range or wire cost dominates.

title: Experiment I: streaming and incremental encode
description:
Hypothesis: Transform-aware accumulation lowers memory and enables progressive input.
Implementation plan: High IFFT accumulator and linear low-profile prototype; finalize subsets.
Correctness oracle: Full ordinary encode bit identity.
Benchmark cells: Blocks, shard sizes, reuse, partial parity.
Promotion threshold: Exact output and >=5% memory/time benefit.
Kill criterion: State/API complexity without measurable benefit.
Final result: pending.

description:
Hypothesis: Block-packed received subsets reduce pruned work.

Benchmark cells: Surplus-received patterns across profiles and bytes.

Kill criterion: Selection setup exceeds saved execution.

description: Experiment D promotion and profile synthesis for GF8 field-boundary rescue. Consolidate C6 results comparing dyadic GF16, direct exact GF8, truncated or epsilon GF8, and low versus high; create a new versioned profile only when useful.

description: Exclusively investigate incremental add remove swap updates to an existing locator plan, including puncture and virtual-erasure cases. Production FWHT sparse and product strategies remain owned by leopard-79h.11.

title: Experiment A: GFNI affine multiplication
description:
Hypothesis: GFNI affine maps reduce fixed GF8 multiplication cost.
Implementation plan: Empirically derive matrices; exhaust all multipliers/inputs; implement XMM/YMM/ZMM variants.
Correctness oracle: Scalar GF8 and nibble-table outputs.
Benchmark cells: Mul, full transforms, and codecs across shard sizes.
Promotion threshold: >=5% target-regime codec gain with no neighbor regression >2%.
Kill criterion: No end-to-end gain after setup/downclock effects.
Final result: pending.
notes: Experiment completed in commit 25ed9b4. Exhaustive 65,536 multiplier/input validation passed for XMM/YMM/ZMM affine, GF2P8MULB-isomorphism, and nibble references; 257-byte tails and ASan/UBSan passed. Pinned two-run 9-sample medians show direct GFNI ZMM codec-like chain gains +7.7% at 1 KiB, +23.2% at 4 KiB, +18.5% at 16 KiB, +0.3% at 64 KiB, but fixed-multiply -2.2% at 16 MiB. Disposition: positive/inconclusive production trial; retain isolated, require size-gated whole-codec validation on additional CPUs before promotion. Evidence docs/leopard2_gfni_affine.md and experiments/leopard2/gfni_affine/. Bead remains open because correctness gate leopard-79h.15 is not yet closed.

Benchmark cells: All transform sizes, ISAs, cache regimes, full codecs.
Promotion threshold: >=5% credible whole-codec gain within code-size budget.
Kill criterion: Spills/i-cache negate gain.
Final result: pending.
